# Review round 7

Branch docs/issue-316-flow-prompt-audit. Findings below are copied verbatim from each reviewer subagent's final report: the section headings (which carry the severity) and every finding row or line that names tier-gate.sh, block-unchecked-merge.sh, block-destructive.sh, command-parse.sh, or their test files. Lines that do not name those files are omitted.

## Final review: security of undo (9456958b..742f470e; labelled round 7 in the main transcript)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-ab9ec8b820534b777.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T17:09:03.686Z

The five allowed suites all pass at 742f470e: e2e-tier-gate 3134 pass, block-unchecked-merge 213, block-destructive-git 143, block-destructive-rm 65, e2e-guard-refusals 365, every one exit 0. No test covers either P1.
## Security Review Findings
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security/injection · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:282`**<br>The new splitting mode (`BD_SPLIT_EXP=1`) breaks a `${...}` that is glued to text before it. It emits that text plus `${NAME:-` as one word, so the flag letters inside the default value lose their dash. For example, `rm -${X:-rf src}` becomes the words `[rm] [-${X:-] [rf] [src]`, while bash, with X unset, runs `[rm] [-rf] [src]`. block-destructive now allows these commands; it blocked all of them at both earlier commits:<br>• `rm -r${X:-f src}`<br>• `rm -r${X:-f }src`<br>• `rm -${X:-rf src}`<br>• `rm -f -${X:-r src}`<br>• `git clean -${X:-f }`<br>• `git clean -${X:-fd }`<br>• `git branch -${X:-D wip}` (wip is unmerged)<br>Results: 45de0559 exit 2, 9456958b exit 2, 742f470e exit 0. Expected: exit 2. _(HIGH)_ | When text is glued before the `${`, keep that text and the first field of the default value together as one word, as bash does. Do the same for text glued after the `}`. The first case would then read `-rf`. If that is not done, fall back to the one-word reading the base used, which blocked every case. Add these commands to block-destructive-rm and block-destructive-git as cases that must be blocked. |
| **SEC-2 · security/injection · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:606-621`**<br>New rule (a), which drops a heredoc body when the introducer is followed by `>` or `\|`, checks quoting only at the end of the line (`q == ""`). It does not check quoting where the match starts. An introducer written inside a quoted string therefore starts a body that does not exist, and tier-gate's `_tg_body_line` (tier-gate.sh:1555) treats the next lone `$CMD` line as body text and stays silent. bash runs that line. Reproduced with bash, X=`echo RAN-CMD`:<br>`echo "To merge, run: cat <<true > notes.md"`⏎`$CMD`⏎`true`<br>The same happens with single quotes: `printf '%s\n' 'Usage: gh pr merge <<EOF \| tee log'`⏎`$CMD`⏎`EOF`.<br>tier-gate results: 9456958b ask, 742f470e silent, 45de0559 silent. Expected: ask, because a lone `$CMD` in text that names merge should ask. This only affects the lone-variable command word. A literal `gh pr merge 7` in such a body still asks. _(HIGH)_ | Take the quote state at RSTART, not at the end of the line, and require it to be empty. The column scan already in this awk program can track it. Add both commands to e2e-tier-gate as cases that must ask. |
| **SEC-3 · security/injection · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:607-608`**<br>Same rule (a). The two `["]?` around the delimiter are each optional on their own, so `<<"EOF > notes.md"` matches with delimiter `EOF`. bash reads the delimiter as `EOF > notes.md`. bash's body therefore ends earlier than the hook's, and the line in between runs:<br>`cat <<"EOF > notes.md"`⏎`release notes`⏎`EOF > notes.md`⏎`$CMD`⏎`EOF`<br>The same applies to `<<EOF" > x"`.<br>tier-gate results: 9456958b ask, 742f470e silent, 45de0559 silent. Expected: ask. _(HIGH)_ | Accept only delimiters whose quotes are balanced (`"NAME"`, `'NAME'`, or bare `NAME`). Anything else keeps its body. |
| **SEC-4 · security/injection · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:487`**<br>Rule (a) trusts `reader_ok`, which is a deny-list of programs that run their input. It has no `sed`. With GNU sed, `sed 'e'` runs each line as a command, so in<br>`cat <<EOF \| sed 'e'`⏎`$CMD`⏎`EOF`⏎`# merge`<br>the `$CMD` line runs. tier-gate results: 9456958b ask, 742f470e silent, 45de0559 silent. This only happens with GNU sed and is close to the known gaps in the shell list, but under your rule it counts as a regression. _(HIGH)_ | Add `sed`, `gsed`, `awk`, `gawk`, `mawk`, `nawk` and `m4` to the reader list, or treat anything that is not a known text sink as a possible runner. That inverts the default. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-5 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh`**<br>Not caused by this diff. These were already present at 9456958b and were not present at 45de0559. Your rule makes a regression against 45de0559 a P1, so these are P1 by the letter. I put them here because this diff did not change them; you decide.<br>• `gh api ${X:- repos/o/r/releases} -f tag_name=v1` and `gh api -X POST ${X:- repos/o/r/releases}`: tier-gate silent at 742f470e and 9456958b, ask at 45de0559. No other hook stops it.<br>• `gh api ${X:- -X PUT} repos/o/r/pulls/7/merge` and `gh api -X PUT ${X:- repos/o/r/pulls/7/merge}`: tier-gate silent at both, ask at 45de0559. block-unchecked-merge blocks them at 742f470e.<br>• `g${X:-h pr merge 7}`: block-unchecked-merge exit 0 at both, exit 2 at 45de0559. tier-gate asks. _(HIGH)_ | When a `gh api` path or method word holds an unquoted `${...}` with whitespace, read it as possibly a merge or release endpoint and ask. |
| **SEC-6 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/block-destructive.sh`**<br>Already present: silent at all three commits. `git reset --hard${X:- }`, `git reset -${X:--hard }` and `git reset --har${X:-d }` all run `git reset --hard`; I checked the argument list bash builds. `git ${X:-reset --hard}`, `git ${X:-branch -D} feat` and `rm ${X:-"-rf"} src` are also silent. _(HIGH)_ | The glue fix in SEC-1 should cover the first three. Add them as must-block cases. |
| **SEC-7 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/block-unchecked-merge.sh`**<br>Already present: exit 0 at all three. `eval "v=\${$n}" >x\`⏎`gh pr merge 7` is joined by the line continuation into `eval ... gh pr merge 7`, which merges. tier-gate asks. _(HIGH)_ | Join continuation lines before reading the segments in this hook. |
### Checked and clean
- **The brief's premise about forced pushes.** `git push --force origin main` returns exit 0 from block-destructive on all three trees. Forced pushes are handled by `block-force-push.sh`, which this diff does not touch and which does not use the shared parser. So nothing changed there, and it is outside this diff.
### Summary
- Overall risk: High. A `rm -rf`, `git clean -f` or force-delete of an unmerged branch written with a glued default value now gets past block-destructive. A lone variable command in text that names merge now gets past tier-gate.

## Final review: code of undo (9456958b..742f470e)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a560e5d413564a9ab.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T17:13:16.469Z

All six named suites pass at that commit (exit status 0). Each finding below was reproduced old against new with the harness at `<scratch>`. In the tables, `tg` is the tier gate's decision, and `bd` and `bum` are the exit status of block-destructive and block-unchecked-merge (2 means refused).
## Code Review Findings
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **F1 · regression · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:606-615`**<br>A merge run from a script that the same command writes with a heredoc used to ask and is now silent. The new heredoc drop calls `reader_ok` on the introducer line only, so a shell on a later line that runs the written file is never checked.<br>Command: `cat <<'EOF' > x.sh` / `CMD="gh pr merge 7"` / `$CMD` / `EOF` / `bash x.sh`<br>Old: `tg=ask`. New: `tg=allow`.<br>The same happens with `CMD="gh pr merge 7" bash x.sh`, with `CMD=... . ./x.sh`, with `chmod +x x.sh; CMD=... ./x.sh`, and with `cat <<'EOF' \| tee x.sh >/dev/null` followed by `bash x.sh`. All five went from ask to allow.<br>This undoes the rule the change states for itself ("`cat <<EOF \| bash` keeps its body"): writing the body to a file and running it on the next line gets past it. No test covers this. _(HIGH)_ | Pass `reader_ok` the whole command, not just `pre " " post`. Or keep the body when a later word is a shell, an interpreter, `.`, `source` or `./`. Then check that the `cat <<EOF > body.md … gh pr create --body-file body.md` row stays silent; it should, because gh is not in `reader_ok`'s list. Add rows for the writes above that end in `ask`. |
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F2 · regression (false ask) · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1591`, `lib/command-parse.sh:379`**<br>`TG_PIPED` is now true for the whole command (`TG_ANYPIPE`). As a result, the argument-position check (`k > $1`) treats any shell name used as an argument as a shell reading a pipe whenever there is a pipe anywhere in the command, including inside `$(...)` or `bash -c '...'`. Separately, `--version` and `--help` hit the `--*) continue` branch and count as reading stdin. Each of these was `allow` before and is now `ask`:<br>• `gh pr list \| wc -l; which bash`<br>• `gh pr list \| grep x; command -v bash`<br>• `bash --version \| head -1 && git --version && gh --version`<br>• `gh pr checks 5 \| tail -3; zsh --version`<br>• `gh auth status 2>&1 \| head -3; echo $SHELL; which bash zsh`<br>• `x=$(ls \| wc -l); which bash; gh pr list`<br>• `bash -c 'ls \| wc -l'; which bash; gh pr list`<br>• `gh pr list \| grep -c x; docker run --rm img sh`<br>The header comment of the `tg-shell-argument` test ("named as an argument (`which bash`) it runs nothing") now holds only for commands with no pipe at all. _(HIGH)_ | Limit the `k > $1` branch to segments that a pipe actually feeds (or to wrapper command words), as before. In `_bd_shell_reads_stdin`, return 1 for `--version`, `--help` and `-V`. Add silent rows for the commands above. |
| **F3 · regression (false refusal) · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:982-990`**<br>`fed` now applies to the whole command, and `quoted` collects every multi-word quoted string from every simple command. One shell command word that the check misreads (`bash --version`) therefore makes unrelated quoted text, such as a commit message, be read as commands.<br>• `git commit -m "fix: refuse git reset --hard in hooks" && bash --version \| head -1`: `bd` 0 → 2 (hard refusal)<br>• `gh pr comment 5 --body "merge with gh pr merge 5 --squash once green" && bash --version \| head -1`: `bum` 0 → 2, `tg` allow → ask _(HIGH)_ | The `--version`/`--help` fix in F2 removes this trigger. Also collect `quoted` only from simple commands that can feed the shell (earlier in a pipeline, or in the same group), not from the whole text. |
| **F4 · regression (false ask) · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1843`**<br>The `-?*` branch matches `*[mMcC]*` on every token, so an option value that starts with `-` is read as `-m` or `-c`. This now sets `hit=1`, which makes every later push ask; before, it only set `up=1`, which affected a push with no remote or refspec.<br>• `git branch --sort -committerdate \| head -5; git push origin feature/issue-42-x`: allow → ask<br>• `git branch --format '-%(refname:short)'; git push origin …`: allow → ask<br>`--sort=-committerdate` (with `=`) stays silent. _(HIGH)_ | Skip the separate value word after `--sort`, `--format`, `--contains`, `--no-contains`, `--merged`, `--no-merged`, `--points-at`, `--abbrev`, `--column` and `-u`/`--set-upstream-to`. |
| **F5 · tests · `plugins/flow/tests/block-unchecked-merge.test.sh`, `e2e-guard-refusals.test.sh`**<br>The new keyword skip in the shared library (`if\|then\|elif\|else\|while\|until\|do\|!\|{`, command-parse.sh:972) is not pinned by any block-destructive or block-unchecked-merge test. I removed it in mutant m7; the full guard-refusals suite (365 pass) and the full merge suite both still pass. Yet the behaviour changes: `echo 'git reset --hard' \| if true; then bash; fi` is refused at HEAD and allowed on m7, and the same holds for `\| until false; do bash; done` and `echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| case x in x) bash ;; esac` (`bum`). Only the tier-gate suite has rows of this kind, and it exercises the tier gate's own scan, not this loop. _(HIGH)_ | Add `\| if true; then bash; fi`, `\| while true; do bash; done`, `\| ! bash` and `\| case x in x) bash ;; esac` rows to both suites. |
### P3 — Consider
| **F7 · pre-existing gap · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:975`**<br>The wrapper list in the piped pass (`sudo\|doas\|env\|nohup\|nice\|time\|command\|builtin\|exec\|timeout\|xargs`) is shorter than the one `reader_ok` uses in the same file (line 487) and shorter than what the tier gate recognises. `echo 'git reset --hard' \| stdbuf -i0 bash` (also with `setsid`, `ionice -c3`, `caffeinate -i`, `busybox sh`, `coproc`) gives `bd=0` in both trees, and the `gh pr merge 7` versions give `bum=0` while the tier gate asks. The diff edits this loop and states that text "printed into a shell … is checked". _(HIGH)_ | Use one wrapper list for both places, the longer one from `reader_ok`. |
### Summary
  - 17 KB `gh pr create --body`: tier gate 3.2s → 2.7s, block-unchecked-merge 1.6s → 1.3s, block-destructive 1.8s → 1.2s.
